questions.prompt: Explain Rust's ownership model. What clicked for you, and what still trips you up?
questions.zh: 解释一下 Rust 的所有权模型。哪一点让你一下子通了？哪一点现在还会绊住你？
outline: One owner per value; assignment moves instead of copying
Borrowing: many readers or one writer, enforced at compile time
Lifetimes describe how long references stay valid
What clicked: treating the borrow checker as a strict pair programmer
Honest limit: my Rust experience is from personal projects, not production
followUps: How do you get out of a borrow checker fight you cannot win?

questions.prompt: How do you handle errors in your Rust projects?
questions.zh: 你的 Rust 项目里怎么处理错误？
outline: Result and Option instead of exceptions; errors are values
The question mark operator propagates with almost no boilerplate
Libraries: a typed error enum with thiserror
Applications: anyhow-style error context at the boundary
unwrap only where a failure is truly impossible, and say why

chunks.zh: 表示“操作可能失败”的返回类型（Rust 用它代替异常）
把错误向上传播（交给调用方处理）
问号运算符（写在表达式后面的 ?）
定义库错误类型的那个库（常和 anyhow 搭配）
错误上下文（给错误加说明）
直接取出里面的值，没有值就崩溃（Option 和 Result 上的方法，u 开头）

followUps: When is panic! acceptable in your code?

questions.prompt: How does async work in Rust, and how is it different from the async you know from other languages?
questions.zh: Rust 的异步是怎么工作的？和你熟悉的其他语言的异步有什么不同？
outline: A future does nothing until something polls it
There is no built-in runtime; my projects use an async runtime like Tokio
Tasks are spawned onto the executor and must not block it
A blocking call inside async code stalls every task on that thread
Send and Sync bounds decide what can cross an await point

chunks.zh: 轮询一个 future（推动它往前执行）
启动一个（异步）任务，s 开头
阻塞执行器（在异步任务里做阻塞操作的后果）
标记类型能否跨线程转移、能否跨线程共享的两个 trait

followUps: What happens if you call a blocking sleep inside an async function?

questions.prompt: Why did you pick Rust for your personal projects — and what are the downsides?
questions.zh: 你为什么选 Rust 做个人项目？它的代价是什么？
outline: Motivation: native performance with memory safety and no garbage collector
Fearless concurrency makes parallel code far less scary
Downsides: compile times and the borrow checker's learning curve
The ecosystem is smaller than Java's or Python's for some tasks
Where I would not pick it: quick scripts — Python wins there

chunks.zh: 在编译期（而不是运行时）
编译耗时（编译要花多长时间，复数）

followUps: Would you use Rust for a CRUD web service at work?

questions.prompt: Explain traits and generics in Rust. When do you use static dispatch, and when dynamic?
questions.zh: 解释一下 Rust 的 trait 和泛型。什么时候用静态分发，什么时候用动态分发？
outline: A trait bound says what a generic type must be able to do
Static dispatch monomorphizes: a specialized copy per type, no runtime cost
A trait object gives dynamic dispatch through a vtable
impl Trait is sugar for generics in argument or return position
Rule of thumb: generics by default, trait objects for heterogeneous collections or plugin points

chunks.zh: trait 约束（限制泛型参数必须实现某个 trait）
隐藏具体类型的写法（用在返回位置）

followUps: What does object safety mean, in plain words?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a real fight you had with the borrow checker in one of your own projects. What did it teach you?
questions.zh: 讲一次你在自己的项目里和借用检查器真正较量过的经历。它教会了你什么？
outline: Personal project, so I could afford to wrestle instead of clone everything
The error looked unreasonable until I drew who owned what
Splitting the struct made the borrows stop overlapping
Cloning was the right call in exactly one hot spot, not everywhere
Now I design ownership first and let the checker review me

chunks.zh: 克隆这个值（显式做一次深拷贝）

followUps: What pattern do you reach for when two parts of a struct need each other?

questions.prompt: When do lifetime annotations stop being automatic in your code? Give me a concrete example.
questions.zh: 在你的代码里，生命周期标注什么时候开始不能靠自动推导了？给个具体例子。
outline: Elision covers the common single-input cases silently
Returning a reference into parsed data forced explicit annotations
The signature had to promise the output outlives nothing it borrows
A dangling reference is the bug the annotation exists to prevent
When the web of borrows grew, I switched to owned data instead

chunks.zh: 生命周期省略（编译器自动推断，不用手写）
比……活得久（生命周期更长），o 开头
'static 生命周期（在整个程序运行期间都有效）

followUps: How do you explain a lifetime to a C++ developer in one sentence?

questions.prompt: Explain Send and Sync like you would to a Java developer. When did they matter in your code?
questions.zh: 像给 Java 开发者讲那样讲讲 Send 和 Sync。它们在你的代码里什么时候真正起过作用？
outline: Send means a value may travel to another thread
Sync means references may be shared across threads safely
The compiler checks them from the types, not from documentation
A non-Send type in my scraper forced a dedicated worker thread
That is fearless concurrency in practice: races become compile errors

chunks.zh: 标记类型能否跨线程转移、能否跨线程共享的两个 trait
数据竞争（多个线程无同步地访问同一块内存，且至少有一个在写）
消息传递（线程之间不共享内存，靠发消息通信）

followUps: Which of your types would you deliberately make not Send?

questions.prompt: When do you reach for interior mutability in Rust, and what does it cost you?
questions.zh: 你什么时候会在 Rust 里用内部可变性？它让你付出了什么代价？
outline: It moves borrow checking from compile time to runtime
A cache inside an otherwise immutable struct was my use case
The cost: a bad access pattern panics instead of failing to compile
Across threads the same idea needs a mutex, not a cell
Smart pointers make the pattern explicit at the type level

chunks.zh: 运行时借用（RefCell 的方式）
把它放进 Box 里（分配到堆上）

followUps: How do you keep runtime borrow panics out of production paths?

questions.prompt: Generics or trait objects: how do you choose in your own code?
questions.zh: 泛型还是 trait 对象：你在自己的代码里怎么选？
outline: Generics monomorphize: fast, but one copy of code per type
Trait objects dispatch dynamically and keep binaries smaller
Object safety rules decide what can even be a trait object
Plugin-style registries pushed me to trait objects once
Default to generics; pay for dynamism only where design needs it

chunks.zh: 对象安全（能否做 trait 对象）

followUps: How does that choice show up in compile times?

questions.prompt: Where would you allow unsafe in a personal project, and how do you fence it in?
questions.zh: 在个人项目里，你会在哪里允许 unsafe？你怎么把它围起来？
outline: Default answer is no unsafe until a profile proves the need
The foreign function interface is the one place it was unavoidable
The safe wrapper states the invariants the raw calls depend on
Undefined behavior is the price of breaking those invariants
Keep the block tiny and let the type system guard the door

chunks.zh: 外部函数接口（FFI 的全称）
在编译期（而不是运行时）

followUps: What would make you reject an unsafe dependency?

questions.prompt: Tell me about debugging an async Rust program that just froze in one of your projects.
questions.zh: 讲一次你调试自己项目里一个直接冻住的异步 Rust 程序的经历。
outline: Symptom: the program hung with no error and low CPU
One task blocked the executor with a long synchronous computation
Other futures were never polled while it held the thread
Moving the work to a spawned blocking task unfroze everything
Lesson: the runtime is cooperative; blocking is a silent contract breach

questions.prompt: Have you written your own macros, or only used them? Walk me through one.
questions.zh: 你写过自己的宏吗，还是只用过别人的？带我看一个。
outline: Honestly: mostly a consumer, through derive macros on my types
Deriving serialization removed pages of handwritten mapping
I wrote one small declarative macro to kill test boilerplate
Procedural macros are a compiler plugin: powerful, slower to build
Rule I follow: a macro must read better than the code it replaces

questions.prompt: Your Rust workspace keeps growing and compile times hurt. What do you do, in order?
questions.zh: 你的 Rust 工作区越长越大、编译时间开始疼了。你按什么顺序处理？
outline: Measure first: which crate and which phase eats the time
Generic-heavy crates monomorphize into long codegen work
Splitting the workspace stops one change from rebuilding the world
Feature flags let debug builds skip heavy optional dependencies
A shared cache across machines was the last, biggest lever

chunks.zh: 编译耗时（编译要花多长时间，复数）

Rust 的包（一个编译单元，也指第三方库），c 开头

followUps: What do you refuse to do for the sake of compile time?

questions.prompt: How do you design errors in a Rust library versus a Rust application?
questions.zh: 在 Rust 里，库和应用的错误设计有什么不同？你怎么做？
outline: Libraries owe callers typed errors they can match on
thiserror keeps those enums honest with little boilerplate
Applications can aggregate with context and print one good message
The question mark operator makes propagation the default path
unwrap is for tests and truly impossible states, never for IO
